source_blueprint_id.description: The id of the blueprint whose steps are appended to the path's blueprint and which is then deleted; it must be of the same team, have no event handler, and leave the result at most 50 steps.

allowed_tools.description: Tools beyond the defaults an agent running the prompt may use, comma-separated, as a SKILL.md file's frontmatter names them, or empty for none.

body.description: The prompt's text, what an agent running it is asked to do.

created_at.description: When the prompt was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

model.description: The model key the prompt runs on, or empty to use the team's default model.

source.description: Where the prompt came from: system for one shipped with Triage Factory, user for one a person created, imported for one imported from a SKILL.md file, or marketplace for one installed from a marketplace listing.

system_slug.description: The stable name of a shipped prompt, absent for any other.

team_id.description: The id of the team that owns the prompt.

updated_at.description: When the prompt was last changed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

usage_count.description: How many agent conversations have run the prompt.

orphaned_blueprint.description: Whether the delete left the steps after the prompt in a new blueprint with no event handler.

status.description: hidden for a shipped or imported prompt, which is hidden from the library, or deleted for one a person created.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

search.description: Narrows to prompts whose name contains this text, compared case-insensitively and literally; trimmed, at most 200 characters, and empty is absent.

team_id.description: Narrows to the prompts of this team; absent is every team the caller can see.

avg_cost_usd.description: The average model spend of a conversation that ran the prompt, in USD.

avg_duration_ms.description: The average working time of a conversation that ran the prompt, in milliseconds.

completed_runs.description: How many of those conversations recorded their step's verdict, or belong to a blueprint run that completed.

failed_runs.description: How many of those conversations failed because the infrastructure under the agent did.

last_used_at.description: When the latest conversation on the prompt started, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null when none has.

runs_per_day.description: How many conversations started on the prompt on each of the last 30 days in UTC, today included, oldest first.

success_rate.description: completed_runs as a share of total_runs, from 0 to 1, or 0 when the prompt has not run.

total_cost_usd.description: The model spend of every conversation that ran the prompt, in USD.

total_runs.description: How many agent conversations have run the prompt.

content.description: The SKILL.md file's text, frontmatter included, at most 256 KiB once trimmed; required.

name.description: The prompt's name; absent or empty is the frontmatter's name, and one of the two is required.

team_id.description: The id of the team to create the prompt under, required when the caller writes to more than one team; absent is the caller's one team.

description.description: The listing's description, or empty for none.

event_types.description: The event types the listing is suited to, ids from GET /api/event-types, which browsing can filter on.

kind.description: What the listing publishes: prompt or blueprint.

name.description: The listing's name, which may not be blank.

source_id.description: The id of the prompt or blueprint to publish, which must have no listing yet; required.

description.description: The listing's description, or empty for none.

event_types.description: The event types the listing is suited to, ids from GET /api/event-types, which replace the listing's current ones.

name.description: The listing's name, which may not be blank.

at_step_index.description: The 0-based index of the first step to move off the path's blueprint to a new one, which must leave at least one step on each side; required.

target_blueprint_id.description: The id of the blueprint whose steps follow the steps the path's blueprint keeps, and which is then deleted; it must be of the same team, have no event handler, and leave the result at most 50 steps. Required.

name.description: The blueprint's new name, trimmed, which may not be empty.

ids.description: The id of every event handler the caller can see, each once, in their new order.

base_branch.description: The branch agents base their work on, absent when they use the default branch.

can_edit.description: Whether the caller may change the repository's settings.

clone_error.description: The output of the failed clone, present only when clone_status is failed.

clone_error_kind.description: What kind of failure the clone hit, ssh or other, present only when clone_status is failed.

clone_status.description: The state of the repository's clone: pending until a clone attempt finishes, then ok or failed.

default_branch.description: The repository's default branch on GitHub, absent before it is profiled.

description.description: The repository's description on GitHub, absent when it has none.

github_id.description: GitHub's id for the repository, empty while it is not yet known.

has_agents_md.description: Whether the repository has an AGENTS.md.

has_claude_md.description: Whether the repository has a CLAUDE.md.

has_readme.description: Whether the repository has a README.

id.description: The repository's id in Triage Factory.

owner.description: The account that owns the repository on GitHub.

profile_text.description: A description of the repository written when it was profiled, absent before then.

profiled_at.description: When the repository was last profiled, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent before then.

repo.description: The repository's name without its owner.

retired_at.description: When the repository was retired because GitHub no longer answers for it, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent on a repository that is not retired.

slug.description: The repository's full name, as owner/name.

base_branch.description: The branch agents base their work on in this repository, or null to clear it so they use the repository's default branch.

fields.description: The fields a predicate for this event type may name, ordered by name.

allowed_tools.description: Tools beyond the defaults an agent running the step may use, comma-separated, or empty for none.

brief.description: Instructions for this step that are added to its prompt, empty for a prompt listing.

model.description: The model key the step runs on, or empty to use the installing team's default model.

at_step_index.description: The 0-based index of the first step to move to the new blueprint, which must leave at least one step on each side; required.

ai_summary.description: A summary of the task written when it was scored, absent before then.

autonomy_suitability.description: How suitable the task is for an agent to work without a person, from 0 to 1, or null before the task is scored.

can_write.description: Whether the caller may update, claim, delegate, or requeue the task, present on the task reads and absent from a write's response or when the check fails.

claim_team_ids.description: The ids of the teams the caller's claim or delegation may put the task on, in order, present on the single-task read only and absent when that read fails.

claimed_by_agent_id.description: The id of the agent that holds the task, absent when no agent does.

claimed_by_user_id.description: The id of the person who holds the task, absent when no person does.

close_reason.description: Why the task closed, such as run_completed, user_completed, user_dismissed, or auto_closed_by_event, absent while it is open.

conversation_id.description: The id of the task's current conversation, absent when nobody holds the task or its run has not started.

created_at.description: When the task was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

dedup_key.description: The value that tells apart tasks of one event type on one entity, such as a label name, absent for most event types.

entity_id.description: The id of the entity the task is about: a pull request, an issue, a vulnerable package, or a Slack thread or message.

entity_kind.description: The kind of entity the task is about: pr, issue, vulnerable_package, thread, or message.

event_type.description: The event type that created the task, such as github:pr:review_requested.

memory_attempt.description: The newest attempt to write that memory, absent when none has run.

memory_pending.description: Whether a conversation on the task ended without the memory the next conversation needs, in which case no further conversation on the task starts until that memory exists.

open_subtask_count.description: How many open subtasks the task's Jira issue has, 0 for any other entity.

priority_reasoning.description: The reasoning behind priority_score, absent before the task is scored.

priority_score.description: How urgently the task needs a person's attention, from 0 to 1, or null before the task is scored.

relevance_reason.description: Why the task concerns the person it was routed to, one of review_requested, authored, mentioned, and assigned, absent when none applies.

requested_reviewer.description: On a github:pr:review_requested task, the requested user's login or the requested team's org/slug, absent on every other task.

scoring_status.description: Where the task is in priority scoring: pending, in_progress, or scored.

severity.description: The task's severity, absent when none is recorded.

snooze_until.description: When a snoozed task returns to the queue, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when the task is not snoozed.

source.description: The system the task's entity comes from, such as github or jira.

source_id.description: The entity's key in its source, such as owner/repo#42 for a pull request or PROJ-123 for a Jira issue.

source_url.description: The entity's page in its source.

status.description: The task's lane: queued, in_progress, done, dismissed, or snoozed.

team_id.description: The id of the team that owns the task, absent while no single team owns it.

version.description: The task's version, which a write to the task must send and which each write raises.

vulnerable_package.description: The package and its open Dependabot alerts on a task whose entity_kind is vulnerable_package, absent on every other task.

closed_since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits done and dismissed tasks to those closed at or after it.

created_before.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits the result to tasks created at or before it.

created_since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits the result to tasks created at or after it.

entity_ids.description: Ids of the entities whose tasks to include, at most 200, each a UUID in lowercase hyphenated form; empty includes every entity.

entity_kinds.description: Entity kinds whose tasks to include, such as pr or vulnerable_package; empty includes every kind.

event_types.description: Event types whose tasks to include, from the catalog GET /api/event-types returns; empty includes every event type.

ids.description: Ids of the tasks to include, at most 200, each a UUID in lowercase hyphenated form; empty includes every task.

include_snoozed.description: Whether to include tasks still inside their snooze window.

only_unclaimed.description: Whether to include only tasks nobody holds.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

search.description: Text the task's title, source id, summary, or event type must contain, matched without regard to case.

sort_dir.description: The direction of sort_key, asc or desc, desc when absent; it is refused without sort_key.

sort_key.description: Orders the result by title, created, event_type, or claimee; absent orders it by the default, open tasks needing attention first and then by priority.

sources.description: Sources whose tasks to include, such as github or jira; empty includes every source.

statuses.description: Lanes to include, from queued, in_progress, done, dismissed, and snoozed; empty includes every lane.

team_ids.description: Ids of the teams whose tasks to include; empty includes every team the caller belongs to.

body.description: The prompt's text, what an agent running it is asked to do; required.

model.description: The model key the prompt runs on, one the deployment offers, or empty to use the team's default model; absent is empty.

cache_creation_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache in the category.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache in the category.

category.description: The spend category: manual for runs a person started, autonomous for runs an event handler started, or system_overhead for background jobs.

cost.description: Spend in the category in USD.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens billed in the category.

output_tokens.description: Output tokens billed in the category.

cost.description: Spend on the day in USD.

date.description: The UTC calendar day, as YYYY-MM-DD.

cost.description: Spend on the model on the day in USD.

date.description: The UTC calendar day, as YYYY-MM-DD.

by_day.description: The caller's spend by UTC day.

by_day_model.description: The caller's spend by UTC day and model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_model.description: The caller's spend by model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

total_cost_usd.description: The caller's total spend in the window in USD.

cost.description: Spend on the model in USD.

category.description: The spend category of spend attributed to no team, such as system_overhead.

cost.description: Spend in the category in USD.

by_day.description: The organization's spend by UTC day.

by_day_model.description: The organization's spend by UTC day and model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_model.description: The organization's spend by model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_rule.description: Spend by the event handler that started each run, present only in local mode.

by_user.description: Spend by the person who started each run, across every team.

org_level.description: Spend attributed to no team, by category.

total_cost_usd.description: The organization's total spend in the window in USD, which equals the sum of by_team and org_level.

cost.description: Spend on the handler's runs in USD.

rule_name.description: The event handler's name, empty when the caller cannot read the handler.

trigger_id.description: The id of the event handler whose runs spent it.

cost.description: Spend attributed to the team in USD.

team_id.description: The team's id.

by_day.description: The team's spend by UTC day.

by_day_model.description: The team's spend by UTC day and model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_model.description: The team's spend by model, leaving out spend attributed to no single model.

by_rule.description: The team's spend by the event handler that started each run.

by_user.description: The team's spend by the person who started each run, present only for a team admin, and an empty array when no person has spend in the window.

team_id.description: The team's id.

total_cost_usd.description: The team's total spend in the window in USD.

avatar_url.description: The URL of the person's avatar, absent when they have none.

cost.description: Spend on the person's runs in USD.

user_id.description: The id of the person who started the runs.

alerts.description: The open alerts, highest severity first and then by number.

ecosystem.description: The package's ecosystem, such as npm or pip.

highest_severity.description: The highest severity among the open alerts, one of low, medium, high, and critical, absent when no open alert has one of those.

open_alert_count.description: How many alerts are open on the package.

active.description: Whether this is the connection the organization uses in the workspace, which is the one whose events are processed.

app_name.description: The Slack app's bot name, empty when Slack gave none.

bot_user_id.description: The Slack user id of the app's bot.

connection.description: The app's live Socket Mode connection status, absent for an app that receives events over HTTP and before the first connection attempt.

connected_at.description: When the connection last opened, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when it has not.

consecutive_failures.description: How many connection attempts in a row have failed.

last_error.description: The error of the last failed attempt, absent when there is none.

last_event_at.description: When the connection last received an event, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when it has not.

sightings.description: Workspaces the app received events from that have no connection in the organization, absent when there are none.

count.description: How many events arrived from the workspace.

last_seen.description: When the last of them arrived, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

team_id.description: The Slack workspace's id.

state.description: The connection's state: dialing, open, draining, backing_off, or auth_failed.

created_at.description: When the connection was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

enterprise_id.description: The id of the Enterprise Grid organization the workspace belongs to, absent for a standalone workspace.

registered_by_user_id.description: The id of the person who connected the app, absent when that person has since been removed.

source.description: Whose Slack app the connection is through: org for an app the organization created, or deployment for the deployment's own app.

transport.description: How Slack delivers the app's events, socket or events_api, or null on a deployment connection, which uses the transport the deployment configures.

updated_at.description: When the connection was last changed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

session.description: The session cookie a browser sign-in sets. A deployment served over plain HTTP names it sid.
session.name: __Host-sid

token.description: An API token, sent as Authorization: Bearer tf_….

get.description: Returns the avatar image of a person in the caller's organization. The image is fetched from the address the person's sign-in provider gave and cached for a short time.

post.description: Returns one page of the blueprint runs the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and most recently started first. Each item is the run itself; GET /api/blueprint-runs/{id} adds its steps.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns one blueprint run with its steps, each with the agent conversation that ran it. The steps are the ones the blueprint had when the run started, whatever has changed in the blueprint since.

post.description: Returns one page of the steps of the blueprints the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and ordered by blueprint id and then step index. Each step carries the version of its blueprint at the time of the read, which a steps replace names.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

post.description: Creates a blueprint on the caller's team and returns it. With first_prompt, it also creates that prompt and makes it the blueprint's one step, and the prompt's name and body are required in place of the blueprint's name.

Copies the named step prompts into new blueprints with no event handler, one for each unbroken run of steps of one blueprint, and leaves the originals as they are. Returns every new blueprint with its steps, as an array.
post.summary: Copy blueprint steps into new blueprints

post.description: Returns one page of the blueprints the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and most recently updated first. A blueprint whose every event handler is for an event type the organization is not licensed for is left out.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

delete.description: Deletes a blueprint and the prompts of its steps. Each event handler that ran the blueprint loses it and stays in place, and one in automate moves to watch.

get.description: Returns one blueprint, in the list's row shape, including one the list leaves out because of the organization's licence.

put.description: Sets a blueprint's name and returns the blueprint. Its steps and its prompts' names are left as they are.

post.description: Appends the source blueprint's steps to the path's blueprint and deletes the source, in one write. The path's blueprint keeps its id, name, and event handlers, and is returned with its steps.

parameters.description: The id of the blueprint that receives the source's steps.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Moves the path's steps from at_step_index on to a new blueprint, then appends the target blueprint's steps to the path's blueprint and deletes the target, in one write. The path's blueprint keeps its id, name, and event handlers, and is returned with its steps and the new blueprint's id.

parameters.description: The id of the blueprint whose steps are reconnected.
parameters.name: id

post.summary: Reconnect a blueprint to another's steps

post.description: Moves the steps from at_step_index on to a new blueprint with no event handler, in one write, and returns both blueprints with their steps. The path's blueprint keeps its id, name, and event handlers.

parameters.description: The id of the blueprint to split.
parameters.name: id

put.description: Sets the order of a blueprint's steps and their briefs, and adds the steps the list names that the blueprint does not hold yet. Returns the blueprint and its steps. The list must name every step the blueprint holds, so removing a step is a prompt delete, and a version the blueprint has moved past is refused.

post.description: Creates an event handler for one event type on the caller's team and returns the stored handler. The Jira and Linear ids a predicate names, such as a status or a priority, are checked against that service, and an event type whose source cannot produce events for the organization is refused.

Returns one page of the event handlers the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and ordered by sort_order and then name. Handlers of an event type the organization is not licensed for are left out, and each handler says whether its event source can produce events for the organization.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

put.description: Rewrites every visible event handler's sort_order to follow the order of ids. The body must name every event handler the caller can see, in every mode, and nothing else.

delete.description: Deletes an event handler, so that no further event matches it. The runs and tasks it already started are left as they are.

get.description: Returns one event handler, in the list's row shape, including one of an event type the organization is not licensed for.

patch.description: Sets the fields the body names on an event handler, leaving the rest as they are, and returns the stored handler. The team and the event type cannot be changed, and the Jira and Linear ids a new predicate names, such as a status or a priority, are checked against that service.

get.description: Returns the predicate fields of every event type the organization is licensed for, as an object keyed by event type. The whole set is returned at once, with no pagination.
Returns the predicate fields of one event type, the fields an event handler's scope_predicate may name. An event type the organization is not licensed for is answered as unknown.

parameters.description: The event type's id, from GET /api/event-types.
parameters.name: event_type

get.description: Returns every event type the organization is licensed for, as an array with no pagination. The set is fixed by the deployment's build.
Reports status ok once the server accepts requests. It needs no credential and checks no database or integration, so it says only that the process is serving.
get.summary: Check that the server is up

post.description: Publishes a copy of one of the caller's team's prompts or blueprints, as it stands now, as a listing every member of the organization can browse, and returns the listing's id. A source that already has a listing, published or delisted, is refused. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.
post.summary: Publish a prompt or blueprint to the marketplace

get.description: Returns the listing published from a prompt or blueprint, whether it is published or delisted. A delisted listing is visible only to members who may write its publishing team. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.

parameters.description: The id of the prompt or blueprint the listing was published from.
parameters.name: source_id

get.summary: Get the marketplace listing of a prompt or blueprint

post.description: Returns one page of the organization's marketplace listings, narrowed by the body's filters and ordered by sort_key, the most installed first by default. A delisted listing is included only for members who may write its publishing team. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns one listing with its counts, the full content of its current version, and its version history. A delisted listing is visible only to members who may write its publishing team. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.

post.description: Hides a listing from every member who may not write its publishing team, so they can no longer browse or install it. Copies already installed from it are left as they are. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.

Copies the current version of a listing into the caller's team as a new prompt or blueprint, and returns the ids of what it created. The copy does not change when the listing is republished, and each install makes a new copy; a delisted listing is refused. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.
post.summary: Install a marketplace listing into a team

post.description: Makes a delisted listing visible to every member of the organization again. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.

Adds a version holding a copy of the listing's source prompt or blueprint as it stands now, sets the listing's name, description, and event types, and returns the listing. Earlier versions are left as they are, and a listing whose source has been deleted is refused. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.
post.summary: Publish a new version of a marketplace listing

delete.description: Removes the caller's vote for a listing. It answers 204 when the caller has no vote there, and for a listing that does not exist. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.
delete.summary: Remove a vote for a marketplace listing

put.description: Records the caller's vote recommending a listing. A vote the caller has already cast is left as it is. Works only in multi mode, and answers 404 in local mode.

get.description: Returns the LLM spend of the runs the caller started in their current organization over the window, in USD, with its totals by category, model, and UTC day.

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

post.description: Returns one page of the organization's Slack connections, active and inactive, ordered by workspace name, then workspace id, then app id. Each connection carries its Socket Mode status when it has one.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns the organization's LLM spend over the window, in USD, with its totals by team, person, category, model, and UTC day, and the spend attributed to no team.

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

post.description: Creates a prompt on the caller's team and returns it. The prompt is part of no blueprint until a blueprint's steps name it.

A scan that fails still answers 200, with the failures in failed and errors. Works only in local mode, and answers 404 in multi mode.
post.summary: Import prompts from the server's skill files

post.description: Returns one page of the prompts the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and most recently updated first.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

post.description: Creates a prompt on the caller's team from a SKILL.md file's text, taking its body and allowed tools from the file, and returns the prompt. The prompt's source is imported.
post.summary: Import a prompt from a SKILL.md file

delete.description: Deletes a prompt and takes it out of its blueprint. A one-step blueprint is deleted with it. In a longer blueprint, the steps after the prompt move to a new blueprint with no event handler, and when the prompt was the first step the blueprint is deleted; a deleted blueprint's event handlers lose their blueprint, and one in automate moves to watch.

get.description: Returns one prompt, in the list's row shape.

put.description: Sets a prompt's name, body, and model, all three of which the body must carry, and returns the prompt.

get.description: Returns counts, cost, and duration over every agent conversation that ran the prompt, and a daily count of those conversations for the last 30 days.

patch.description: Sets or clears the branch agents base their work on in the repository, and returns the repository with the change applied.

parameters.description: The repository's id in Triage Factory.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Returns one page of the tasks the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and ordered by sort_key, or without one by attention and then priority. Each task says whether the caller may write it. A page_token resumes after the last task of the page that returned it, and is refused for different filters.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

delete.description: Removes a person from the team. A caller who names their own id leaves the team, and the team's last admin cannot be removed.

parameters.description: The id of the person to remove.
parameters.name: user_id

get.description: Returns the team's LLM spend over the window, in USD, with its totals by category, event handler, model, and UTC day. The totals by person are included only for a team admin.

parameters.description: The team's id, or default for the one team in local mode.
parameters.name: team_id

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

get.description: Upgrades the connection to a websocket that streams events for the caller in their current organization, such as a changed task list or a run's new messages. Most events say only that a resource changed, and the client reads it again through its route.
